newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh police storm prison, five inmates dead.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh police storm prison, five inmates dead.

text.p: Security forces used teargas, water cannon and a bulldozer to storm a prison in Bangladesh on Sunday, crushing a revolt by inmates in fighting which left at least five prisoners dead, police said.

Up to 50 other prisoners and 11 officers were injured when security forces raided the prison in Jessore early on Sunday, crashing through the prison gates and a barricade erected inside by inmates before rounding up some 2,700 mutineers.
The raid ended the week-long uprising, the last of four which broke out across the country in the past week.

"The securitymen encountered resistance by prisoners armed with knives and iron rods. There was a brief fight in which several prisoners and a few of our forces were injured," one police officer told Reuters by telephone.
Other sources in Jessore said the death toll could be higher. Doctors in the local hospital said scores of people had been treated but they declined to give the number of casualties.
The Jessore prisoners began their revolt on Monday, setting off unrest in three other prisons, including the high-security Dhaka central jail.
"The jail mutiny has ended with the fall of the Jessore jail," the police officer said.

The mutiny was triggered by the release of 90 prisoners under an amnesty marking the country's 25th independence anniversary on Monday. Prisoners, angered at being excluded from the amnesty, demanded freedom while others sought better treatment and food.
On Friday, prisoners in the Dhaka central jail rebelled but were overpowered by guards after a brief fight in which 15 guards and 35 inmates were injured.
The revolt in northwestern Tangail town by prisoners who kept six guards and officials hostage ended peacefully on Thursday after a local politician persuaded them to return to their cells.
A mutiny in southern Barisal jail on Thursday was suppressed within an hour by security forces.
